title: Bank of England Decision Maker Panel monthly data (September 2026) — the firm-expectations survey the July MPC minutes cite by name, published London morning on US-payrolls Friday
source: EST: bankofengland.co.uk/decision-maker-panel/2026/september-2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the Bank's own September-2026 DMP page carries no data and states verbatim 'This monthly Decision Maker Panel data will be published on 2 October 2026.' Corroborated from two further primaries fetched the same day: the August-2026 DMP release page (bankofengland.co.uk/decision-maker-panel/2026/august-2026, 'Published on 04 September 2026') carries 'Next Release: 2 October 2026', and the panel's own site decisionmakerpanel.co.uk states 'Next month's Decision Maker Panel data release - 2nd October 2026'. Primary-sourced from the publisher's own schedule; filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts carries FED: for the Federal Reserve and has no slot for a non-Fed central bank — the same gap boe-decision-2026-09-17, ecb-decision-2026-09-10 and boj-decision-2026-09-18 were filed under. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/boe-dmp-2026-10-02.from-uk-labour-market-2026-09-15.json (read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). The proposal's PLACEMENT finding stands and is carried: this release lands between boe-decision-2026-09-17 and boe-decision-2026-11-05 and before uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28, so it is the first firm-expectations read published after the September vote. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH CHANGED: the proposal named the wrong cell. It framed the DMP as 'firms' own expected wage growth one year ahead, the MPC's forward wage survey'; the committee's own July 2026 minutes (bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy-summary-and-minutes/2026/july-2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09) cite something else, verbatim: 'own-price expectations in the DMP survey, wage-price feedback and food inflation, pointed to a likelihood of limited second-round effects to come.' OWN-PRICE expectations are the load-bearing cell, not the wage cell. SECOND FINDING — this print is structurally incapable of surprising, on two mechanisms both read off primaries: every headline figure is reported as a THREE-MONTH MOVING AVERAGE (the BoE's own release wording, 'in the three months to August'), so two of the 10-02 release's three months were already published on 09-04; and the panel rotates, decisionmakerpanel.co.uk/about-the-panel verbatim 'Each month we send one of three sets of questions to one third of the panel members', against ~10,400 panel firms and 2,012 August respondents. THIRD FINDING — the DMP publication calendar is opaque beyond one release and has already broken its own monthly pattern in 2026: July-2026 data was published 24 July 2026 (same month, fieldwork 3-17 July, 1,982 responses) and the next release was not until 4 September 2026 — a six-week gap with no August publication. Whether a public DMP lands before the 11-05 MPC decision and Monetary Policy Report is therefore NOT KNOWABLE today; the 10-02 release's own 'next release' line is what answers it. LATEST DATA (August 2026 release, published 2026-09-04, fieldwork 7-21 August, 2,012 responses, all three-month averages): expected own-price growth year-ahead 3.8% (-0.1pp); realised own-price growth 3.7% (-0.1pp); CPI expectations one year ahead 3.1%, down from 3.4% in the three months to July and 3.7% in the three months to June; CPI expectations three years ahead 2.8%, unchanged; realised wage growth 4.0%, unchanged; expected wage growth year-ahead 3.4%, flat for two releases; realised employment growth -0.2% (up from -0.4%); expected employment growth +0.1%. Energy-shock supplementary questions: 59% of firms expect to raise prices (down 5pp since April, i.e. April 64%) versus 55% in the July release — a 4pp RE-ACCELERATION, the one cell in this survey moving toward the three dissenters; 61% expect lower profit margins, down from 68%; on wages, 19% expect energy costs to push wages up against 17% down. Tiered LOW and argued, not inherited: UK-only, symbols: [], no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed, no measured tape reaction to any DMP release exists in this book, and the two damping mechanisms above make a surprise structurally unlikely. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action. Corridor on the day: jobs-2026-10-02 (US non-farm payrolls, 08:30 ET, high) lands hours AFTER a London-morning release, with eurostat-hicp-flash, google-adtech-final-judgment-2026-10-02 and m3-full-report-2026-10-02 the same day, and government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30 two days before.
